mainTopic: Honoring שבת in speech, walking and clothing, with aggadic digressions on eating earth, מגילת רות, and the burning of סנחריב's army.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the פסוק in ישעיה about honoring שבת. Speaking about weekday business on שבת is forbidden, though thinking about it is allowed. רבא rejects the first explanation of 'weekday walking', which was jumping over a stream, so the גמרא explains it as taking large strides instead. A second question of רבי, about eating earth, leads to a ruling that it is forbidden every day because it is harmful, and to aggadic sayings about the dead of the מבול buried in בבל. The גמרא then reads נעמי's instruction to רות to 'put on your robes' as referring to שבת clothes. This opens a long series of דרשות of רבי אלעזר on מגילת רות: the wisdom of רות and שמואל, why בועז noticed רות, and hints in his words about בית דוד, מנשה, and the eras of blessing that would come from her. Next, three אמוראים argue about 'ותחת כבודו', the burning of סנחריב's army: did the body burn but not the clothes, did the body itself burn, or did the soul burn while the body stayed whole? The amud ends as a new teaching of רבי יוחנן begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Shabbat speech must differ from weekday speech
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the phrase 'ודבר דבר' to mean that Shabbat speech should not be like weekday speech. Speaking about weekday matters is forbidden, but thinking about them is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: That your speech on Shabbat should not be like your speech on a weekday. Speaking is forbidden; thinking is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the פסוק in ישעיה about honoring Shabbat. Here it explains the part about speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ודבר דבר' teach that you should not talk about your weekday business on Shabbat. The rule only covers speaking out loud. Merely thinking about those matters (הרהור) is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the halacha that one should not discuss weekday business on Shabbat, while thinking about it is not forbidden.

phrases.english: That your speech of Shabbat should not be
like your speech of the weekday.
Speech is forbidden; thinking is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דִּבּוּרְךָ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת כְּדִבּוּרְךָ שֶׁל חוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the exposition of the פסוק from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Talking about weekday matters on Shabbat is forbidden; thinking about them is permitted.

steps.title: What does 'Shabbat walking unlike weekday walking' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it understands all the other parts of the exposition. It asks what is meant by 'your walking on Shabbat should not be like your weekday walking.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, all the others are fine. But 'that your walking on Shabbat should not be like your walking on a weekday': what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the other explanations but asks for the meaning of one unclear phrase about walking. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Speech and the other items have clear meanings. 'Walking differently' is vague, so the גמרא needs a concrete case that shows what kind of walking is a problem on Shabbat.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? What does it mean?

phrases.english: Granted, all of them are fine,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הִילּוּכְךָ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: but 'that your walking of Shabbat should not be
like your walking of the weekday', what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כּוּלְּהוּ — לְחַיֵּי, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the speech phrase to the unclear walking phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of forbidden 'weekday walking' on Shabbat.

steps.title: First answer: jumping over a stream
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, in the name of רב (or רבי אבא in the name of רב הונא), says that if someone on Shabbat reaches a stream, he may cross it only if he can step across normally. If he would have to jump, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like what רב הונא said in the name of רב, and some say רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא: If someone was walking on Shabbat and reached a stream of water, then if he can put down his first foot before lifting the second, it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a case. Jumping over a stream counts as forbidden 'weekday walking.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stream is narrow enough to cross with a normal step, where one foot lands before the other leaves the ground, that is fine. If crossing requires a jump, it is the kind of energetic weekday movement that does not fit Shabbat.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (a different chain of transmission)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Like that which Rav Huna said that Rav said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: Two versions of who said it.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בְּשַׁבָּת וּפָגַע בְּאַמַּת הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: If one was walking on Shabbat and came upon a stream of water,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לְהַנִּיחַ אֶת רַגְלוֹ רִאשׁוֹנָה
phrases.english: if he can put down his first foot
before the second is lifted, it is permitted,
and if not, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Meaning he would have to jump.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forbidden weekday walking means jumping over a stream.

steps.title: רבא objects: what else can he do?
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that the person has no good alternative. Going around adds walking, and walking through the water risks soaked clothes and wringing them out. So jumping must be permitted here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: What should he do? If he goes around, he is adding to his walking. If he walks through, sometimes his clothes get soaked with water and he will come to wring them out. Rather, in this case, since there is no other way, it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב הונא's answer by showing that the person facing the stream has no better option. He concludes that jumping is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every alternative is worse. Going around means extra exertion, and wading through could lead to סחיטה, the מלאכה of wringing. Since jumping is the least problematic choice, it cannot be the example of forbidden weekday walking.

keyTerms.meaning: Wringing out (a forbidden מלאכה on Shabbat)
It is fine; it is permitted

phrases.english: Rava objected to it: What should he do?
Go around? He increases his walking.
Walk through? Sometimes his clothes get soaked with water,
and he will come to wringing.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּהָא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: Rather, in this case, since it is not possible otherwise, it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רָבָא: הֵיכִי לֶיעְבֵּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and overturns the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that jumping over a stream is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All the alternatives are worse, so jumping must be permitted. It therefore cannot illustrate forbidden walking.

steps.title: Second answer: taking large steps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא instead explains weekday walking as taking large steps. It cites רבי's question to רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי. He answered that large steps are not even allowed on weekdays, since they damage 1/500 of a person's eyesight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like what רבי asked רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי: May one take large steps on Shabbat? He said to him: And on a weekday is it permitted? For I say: a large step takes away one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer failed, the גמרא gives a new answer to the question of step 2: weekday walking means taking large, hurried strides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Large strides are the typical rushed walking of the workweek, so they are inappropriate on Shabbat. רבי ישמעאל adds that such steps are harmful even on weekdays, because they weaken eyesight.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it even permitted on a weekday?
The light of his eyes; his eyesight

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל's reply does not mean the rule has nothing to do with Shabbat. The גמרא uses this case to define Shabbat walking, and he simply adds that large steps are harmful on any day.

phrases.english: Rather, as Rabbi asked
of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:
What is the law about taking a large step on Shabbat?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי בַּחוֹל מִי הוּתְּרָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: And on a weekday is it permitted?
For I say: a large step takes away

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מֵחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת מִמְּאוֹר עֵינָיו שֶׁל אָדָם.
phrases.english: one five-hundredth of a person's eyesight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּדִבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 3 with a new answer to step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidden walking meant jumping over a stream.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forbidden walking means taking large strides.
steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation of 'Shabbat walking unlike weekday walking' is: do not take large strides on Shabbat.

steps.title: Eyesight restored at Friday-night קידוש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the eyesight lost through large steps is restored during קידוש on Friday night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is restored to him through the קידוש of שבת evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short comforting note to רבי ישמעאל's statement: the lost eyesight comes back through קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damage from the hurried weekday pace is repaired when Shabbat begins with קידוש. The גמרא presents this as a remedy for the harm רבי ישמעאל described; it does not give it as a new reason for the Shabbat rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is returned to him
The קידוש of Shabbat evening (at twilight)

phrases.english: And it is restored to him through the kiddush of Shabbat evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַהְדַּר לֵיהּ בְּקִידּוּשָׁא דְּבֵי שִׁמְשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a remedy to the harm described in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eyesight lost through large steps is restored at Friday-night קידוש.

steps.title: רבי asks: may one eat earth on Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי a second question: may one eat earth on Shabbat?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי asked רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי: May one eat earth on Shabbat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another question the same two חכמים discussed. This sets up a parallel answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People ate earth as a remedy, so the question may concern רפואה on Shabbat. The answer will follow the same pattern as the previous one.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi asked of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei:
What is the law about eating earth on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי מֵרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question by the same questioner, related by association.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eating earth is allowed on Shabbat.

steps.title: Forbidden even on weekdays because it is harmful
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that eating earth is forbidden even on weekdays, because it causes illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And on a weekday is it permitted? For I say: even on a weekday it is forbidden, because it is harmful.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל uses the same reply style as before: the act is forbidden every day, not only on Shabbat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban has nothing to do with Shabbat. It is based on health, since earth makes a person sick. So there is no special Shabbat question here.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי בַּחוֹל מִי הוּתְּרָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: And on a weekday is it permitted?
For I say: even on a weekday it is forbidden,
because it is harmful.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי בַּחוֹל מִי הוּתְּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Eating earth is forbidden every day because it is harmful.

steps.title: רבי אמי: eating the earth of בבל is like eating ancestors
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says that whoever eats the earth of בבל is as if eating the flesh of his ancestors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Anyone who eats from the earth of בבל, it is as if he eats from the flesh of his ancestors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a strong statement against eating earth, specifically the earth of בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Generations of ancestors were buried in בבל, so its soil is mixed with their remains. This gives an extra reason to avoid eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: The dust or earth of בבל

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
Anyone who eats from the earth of Babylonia,
it is as if he eats from the flesh of his ancestors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: כָּל הָאוֹכֵל מֵעֲפָרָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further statement about eating earth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the earth of בבל is like eating one's ancestors.

steps.title: Another view: like eating creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: Others say eating the earth of בבל is like eating שקצים ורמשים, based on the פסוק about the מבול wiping out all living things.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: as if he eats שקצים and רמשים, as it is written: 'And He wiped out all that existed...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the statement, with a different comparison and a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All creatures, including creeping ones, died in the מבול. As the next steps explain, their remains were swept into בבל, so its soil is mixed with forbidden creatures.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כְּאִילּוּ אוֹכֵל שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים,
phrases.english: And some say: as if he eats abominations and creeping creatures,
as it is written: 'And He wiped out all that existed, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: כְּאִילּוּ אוֹכֵל שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative version of רבי אמי's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the earth of בבל is like eating שקצים ורמשים, which died in the מבול.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: why בבל is called שנער
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that בבל is called שנער because all who died in the מבול were swept (ננערו) there.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Why is it called שנער? Because all the dead of the מבול were shaken off there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an aggadic statement explaining why the dead of the מבול ended up in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name שנער is read as a play on 'ננערו', meaning 'were shaken out'. This supports the idea that בבל's soil contains the remains of the מבול.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who died in the Flood

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Why is its name called 'Shinar'?
Because all the dead of the Flood were shaken out there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ שִׁנְעָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 10 with a name derivation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שנער means the place where the dead of the מבול were swept.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: why בבל is called מצולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that בבל is called מצולה because all who died in the מבול sank (נצטללו) there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why is it called מצולה? Because all the dead of the מבול sank there.
steps.whatsHappening: A parallel name derivation from רבי יוחנן makes the same point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מצולה, meaning 'depths', is linked to 'נצטללו', meaning 'sank down'. Like ריש לקיש's derivation, it places the remains of the מבול in בבל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Why is its name called 'Metzula'?
Because all the dead of the Flood sank there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמָהּ מְצוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel to step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצולה means the place where the dead of the מבול sank.

steps.title: But those creatures have surely decomposed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'some say' view. Those creatures have certainly decomposed long ago, so eating the earth should not count as eating שקצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say 'as if he eats שקצים ורמשים': but surely they have completely decomposed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the logic of step 10. Remains that have fully decayed are no longer forbidden creatures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that has rotted into dust has lost its identity as a forbidden food. So the comparison to eating שקצים seems wrong, and a different reason for the ban is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They have completely dissolved or decomposed

phrases.english: [And some say: as if he eats] abominations and creeping creatures,
but surely they have completely decomposed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא וַדַּאי אִיתְמַחוֹיֵי אִיתְמַחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to challenge the view of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that eating the earth of בבל is like eating שקצים ורמשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fully decomposed remains are no longer forbidden, so there should be no איסור of שקצים.

steps.title: חכמים decreed because earth is harmful
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the ban is not really about שקצים. Since earth is harmful, חכמים made a decree against eating it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Since it is harmful, the חכמים made a decree about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. The real reason for the ban is health, through a rabbinic decree (גזירה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'שקצים' statement is only a strong expression, not the actual legal basis. The halachic reason is the danger of earth, which matches רבי ישמעאל's 'מפני שהוא מלקה' in step 8.

phrases.english: They say: since it is harmful,
the Sages decreed against it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי כֵּיוָן דְּמַלְקֵי גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the basis of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating earth is forbidden because it contains the remains of שקצים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a rabbinic decree based on the physical danger.
steps.whatToRemember: The halachic reason not to eat earth is health danger, through a גזירה of חכמים.

steps.title: The man who died from earth and cress
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the danger. A man ate earth and also ate cress. The cress grew inside him, pierced his heart, and he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: For there was a certain man who ate earth and ate cress, and the cress sprouted against his heart, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the decree with a real incident that shows how dangerous eating earth can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earth inside him acted like soil, so the cress seeds took root and grew until they pierced his heart. This tragedy is presented as the event behind the חכמים' decree.

phrases.english: For there was a certain man who ate clay
and ate cress,
and the cress sprouted into his heart, and he died.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּאֲכַל גַּרְגִּישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the decree of step 14 with an incident.
steps.raayaObject: The decree against eating earth because it is harmful.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of a man who died after eating earth and cress.

steps.title: נעמי's 'robes' are שבת clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the clothing נעמי told רות to put on refers to special שבת garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And you shall bathe, anoint yourself, and put on your robes." רבי אלעזר said: These are שבת clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the theme of special שבת clothing and quotes רבי אלעזר, who reads a פסוק in רות as referring to שבת garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רות surely already had clothing on, so telling her to 'put on your robes' suggests special clothes. רבי אלעזר says these were her שבת clothes, worn to honor an important occasion. This fits the earlier lesson that one should have special clothing for שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the theme of honoring שבת with special clothing to a פסוק in תנ"ך.

phrases.english: "And you shall bathe, and anoint yourself, and put on your robes"
Rabbi Elazar said:
These are Shabbat garments.
phrases.notes: Since she was already dressed, 'your robes' means special clothes

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵלּוּ בְּגָדִים שֶׁל שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of eating earth and returns to the earlier theme of honoring שבת with clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'robes' in רות 3:3 are שבת garments.

steps.title: רות and שמואל are the wise who become wiser
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the פסוק 'Give to the wise and he will become wiser' refers to רות and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Give to a wise person and he will become even wiser." רבי אלעזר said: This is רות the Moabite and שמואל from Ramah.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we are already talking about רות, the גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אלעזר. It names two people who took advice and made it even better, and the next steps will explain this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משלי describes a wise person who gets instructions and adds his own wisdom to them. רבי אלעזר says רות and שמואל are examples. This step is only the claim, and the proof for each person comes in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Give to the wise and he will become wiser (משלי 9:9)

phrases.english: "Give to the wise one and he will become wiser"
Rabbi Elazar said:
This refers to Ruth the Moabite and Samuel of Ramah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: זוֹ רוּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּה וּשְׁמוּאֵל הָרָמָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with another רבי אלעזר teaching connected to רות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רות and שמואל are examples of wise people who improved on the instructions they received.

steps.title: רות changed the order of נעמי's instructions
steps.stepSummary: נעמי told רות to get dressed up and then go down to the threshing floor, but רות went down first and only then did what she was told.
steps.simpleTranslation: רות: נעמי told her, "Bathe, anoint yourself, put your robes on, and go down to the threshing floor." But about רות herself it says, "She went down to the threshing floor," and only after that, "She did all that her mother-in-law commanded."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רות added wisdom by showing that she changed the order of נעמי's instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נעמי's order was to get dressed up first and then go. The פסוק shows רות went first and got ready only when she arrived. רש"י explains she did not want to walk on the road dressed up and perfumed, so people would not suspect her of improper behavior.
steps.confusionAlert: רות did not disobey נעמי. She did everything נעמי asked, only in a wiser order.

phrases.english: Ruth: whereas Naomi said to her
"And you shall bathe, and anoint yourself, and put your robes upon you
and go down to the threshing floor,"
phrases.notes: Getting ready comes first, then going

phrases.english: but about her herself it is written: "And she went down to the threshing floor,"
and only afterward: "And she did according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her."
phrases.notes: She got ready only after arriving, to avoid suspicion on the road

steps.triggerLanguage: רוּת, דְּאִילּוּ נָעֳמִי קָאָמְרָה לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first half of רבי אלעזר's claim, about רות.
steps.raayaObject: That רות added wisdom to the instructions she received.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The difference in order between רות 3:3 and רות 3:6.

steps.title: שמואל left out God's Name until he was sure
steps.stepSummary: עלי told שמואל to answer 'Speak, ה׳', but שמואל answered only 'Speak', without the Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל: עלי told him, "Lie down, and if He calls you, say: Speak, ה׳, for Your servant is listening." But about שמואל it says, "ה׳ came and stood and called as before: שמואל, שמואל. And שמואל said: Speak, for Your servant is listening." He did not say "Speak, ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that שמואל also added wisdom, because he did not follow עלי's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עלי told him to say God's Name in his answer. שמואל left the Name out, since he was not yet sure the voice was really from ה׳ and did not want to say the Name for nothing. Like רות, he kept the instruction but improved it.

keyTerms.meaning: עלי, the כהן גדול who raised שמואל
Speak, for Your servant is listening

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's point: רות changed the order and שמואל changed the wording. Both obeyed, but with extra wisdom.

phrases.english: Samuel: whereas Eli said to him
"Lie down, and if He calls you

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַרְתָּ דַּבֵּר ה׳ כִּי שׁוֹמֵעַ עַבְדֶּךָ״,
phrases.english: you shall say: Speak, Lord, for Your servant is listening,"
but about him himself it is written:
"And the Lord came and stood
and called as at the other times: Samuel, Samuel

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל דַּבֵּר כִּי שֹׁמֵעַ עַבְדֶּךָ״,
phrases.english: and Samuel said: Speak, for Your servant is listening,"
and he did not say "Speak, Lord."
phrases.notes: He was not yet certain it was God

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאִילּוּ עֵלִי קָאֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second half of רבי אלעזר's claim, about שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל added wisdom to עלי's instruction.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The difference in wording between שמואל א 3:9 and 3:10.

steps.title: רות searched for decent people to walk with
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains the doubled wording 'she went and she came' as רות going back and forth until she found proper people to go with.
steps.simpleTranslation: "She went, and she came, and she gleaned in the field." רבי אלעזר said: She went and came, went and came, until she found decent people to go along with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אלעזר about רות, explaining extra words in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'she went to the field.' The extra 'and she came' teaches that she went back and forth many times. She was looking for proper, decent people to go with so she would not be alone with improper company.

phrases.english: "And she went, and she came, and she gleaned in the field"
Rabbi Elazar said:
that she went and came, went and came,
until she found suitable people
to walk with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שֶׁהָלְכָה וּבָאת, הָלְכָה וּבָאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of רבי אלעזר's readings of רות chapter 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled 'went and came' shows that רות searched for decent company.

steps.title: Why would בועז ask about a young woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why בועז, a great and holy man, would ask about a young woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And בועז said to his servant who was in charge of the harvesters: Whose young woman is this?" Was it really בועז's way to ask about young women?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty on the פסוק, and the next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great צדיק like בועז would not normally take an interest in a young woman. So the question 'Whose is she?' seems out of character. Something must have drawn his attention.

keyTerms.meaning: בועז, the owner of the field, who later married רות
Was it really his way? (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: "And Boaz said to his servant
who was standing over the harvesters
To whom does this young woman belong?"

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי דַרְכּוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעַז לִשְׁאוֹל בְּנַעֲרָה?
phrases.english: Was it Boaz's habit to inquire about a young woman?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דַרְכּוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעַז לִשְׁאוֹל בְּנַעֲרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק in רות chapter 2 and questions it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It does not fit בועז's character to ask about a young woman, so there must be a deeper reason.

steps.title: בועז saw her wisdom in the הלכות of לקט
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that בועז saw רות acting wisely by the הלכה: she took two fallen stalks but not three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: He saw wisdom in her. Two stalks she picked up, three stalks she did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question: בועז was impressed by רות's knowledge of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה of לקט is that one or two stalks that fall during harvest belong to the poor, but three stalks together stay with the owner. רות followed this exactly, which showed she knew תורה. That is why בועז asked about her.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter of wisdom (here: knowing הלכה)
Fallen stalks that belong to the poor

steps.confusionAlert: Her taking only two is not modesty or shyness. It is following the exact הלכה of לקט.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
He saw in her a matter of wisdom.
Two stalks, she would collect;
phrases.notes: One or two fallen stalks are לקט for the poor

phrases.english: three stalks, she would not collect.
phrases.notes: Three together still belong to the owner

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: דְּבַר חָכְמָה רָאָה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a hidden reason for בועז's question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בועז seemed to be taking an inappropriate interest in a young woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was impressed by her precise knowledge of the הלכות of לקט.

steps.title: A ברייתא says בועז saw her modesty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a different answer: בועז noticed רות's צניעות in how she gathered the stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: He saw modesty in her. Stalks still standing she picked while standing, and fallen stalks she picked while sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different answer to why בועז asked about רות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, what caught בועז's eye was her צניעות, not her knowledge. She did not bend over to pick up fallen stalks. Instead she sat down to pick them up, which is a more modest way to move.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
He saw in her a matter of modesty:
upright stalks, she picked while standing;
fallen stalks, she picked while sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: דְּבַר צְנִיעוּת רָאָה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation, alongside רבי אלעזר's, for בועז's question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בועז's question seems out of character.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was impressed by her modest way of gathering.

steps.title: Why would בועז tell her to cling close?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why בועז would use the word 'cling' about a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And so shall you cling to my maidens." Was it really בועז's way to cling to women?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another difficulty on a פסוק, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cling' is a strong word of closeness. It seems strange for a צדיק like בועז to invite such closeness with women, even through his maidens. The גמרא wants to know why he chose this word.

phrases.english: "And so shall you cling to my maidens"

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעַז לִדָּבֵק עִם הַנָּשִׁים?
phrases.english: Was it Boaz's habit to cling to women?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעַז לִדָּבֵק עִם הַנָּשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 21, applied to the next פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such closeness with women does not fit בועז's character.

steps.title: רות's loyalty made it proper to cling to her
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that since בועז knew רות 'clung' to נעמי, he felt it was permitted to be close to such a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Since he saw "ערפה kissed her mother-in-law, but רות clung to her," he said: It is permitted to cling to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by connecting the word 'cling' to an earlier פסוק about רות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערפה said goodbye to נעמי, but רות 'clung' to her and refused to leave. Seeing such loyalty and righteousness, בועז felt that clinging to someone like this is a good thing and permitted. The same word 'cling' links the two פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: ערפה, the other daughter-in-law who went back

steps.whatToRemember: Every time בועז seems to act out of character, רבי אלעזר shows it was because of a special quality in רות: her wisdom, her modesty, or her loyalty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Since he saw
"And Orpah kissed her mother-in-law
but Ruth clung to her,"
he said: It is permitted to cling to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Links the word 'cling' to an earlier פסוק showing רות's character.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בועז seemed to invite improper closeness.
steps.terutzMaskana: רות's loyalty to נעמי showed she was someone worth being close to, so it was permitted.

steps.title: The word 'here' hints at the kingship of דוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that when בועז told רות 'come here' (הלם), he was hinting that בית דוד would come from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And בועז said to her at mealtime: Come here.' רבי אלעזר said: He hinted to her that the kingship of בית דוד would come from her, because the word 'here' is used about דוד's kingship: 'דוד המלך came and sat before God and said: Who am I, my Lord God, and what is my family, that You have brought me to here?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next verse in רות and gives רבי אלעזר's reading: the simple word 'הלם' is a hidden hint to דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is the shared word 'הלם'. The word appears when דוד thanks ה׳ for bringing him and his kingship 'עד הלם'. So when בועז says 'גשי הלם' to רות, רבי אלעזר hears a hint: 'kingship will come to you'.

keyTerms.meaning: He hinted a hint to her (a hidden message inside plain words)
Here (to this place); the word that links to David's kingship
The kingship of the House of David

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיֹּאמֶר לָה בֹעַז לְעֵת הָאֹכֶל גֹּשִׁי הֲלֹם״ —
phrases.english: "And Boaz said to her at mealtime: Come here"
Rabbi Elazar said,
He hinted a hint to her:

phrases.aramaic: עֲתִידָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד לָצֵאת מִמֵּךְ,
phrases.english: The kingship of the House of David will in the future come out from you,
for the word "here" is written about it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיָּבֹא הַמֶּלֶךְ דָּוִד וַיֵּשֶׁב לִפְנֵי ה׳
phrases.english: as it says: "And King David came and sat before God

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר מִי אָנֹכִי אֲדֹנָי ה׳ וּמִי בֵיתִי
phrases.english: and said: Who am I, my Lord God, and what is my family
that You have brought me to here?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, רֶמֶז רָמַז לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of דרשות on בועז's words to רות, moving on to the next verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הלם' hints that the kingship of בית דוד will come from רות.

steps.title: Vinegar is good in hot weather
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from 'dip your bread in vinegar' that vinegar is good during a heat wave.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And dip your bread in vinegar.' רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that vinegar is good in hot weather.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the verse, and רבי אלעזר draws a simple practical health lesson from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the previous hint, this is a plain-meaning lesson. The harvest happened in the hot season, and בועז offered vinegar, so it must be refreshing in the heat.

phrases.english: "And dip your bread in vinegar,"
Rabbi Elazar said:
From here we see that vinegar is good in hot weather.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vinegar is beneficial in hot weather.

steps.title: Vinegar hints at the harsh king מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads the vinegar as a hint that a descendant with 'sharp' deeds, מנשה, would come from רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: He hinted to her that a son would come from her whose actions are harsh like vinegar. And who is he? מנשה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reading of the same words: the vinegar is not health advice but a hint about a future wicked king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vinegar is sharp and sour, so it stands for harsh, bad deeds. The descendant is מנשה, the wicked king of יהודה. This balances the good hint about דוד with a warning that not all her descendants would be righteous.

keyTerms.meaning: מנשה, a wicked king of יהודה, descended from דוד

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
He hinted a hint to her
that a son will in the future come out from you
whose actions are harsh like vinegar,
and who is he? Menashe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: רֶמֶז רָמַז לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same 'vinegar' words that רבי אלעזר explained in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vinegar hints at מנשה, a descendant with harsh deeds.

steps.title: Sitting beside the harvesters hints that דוד's kingdom will split
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר notes that רות sat 'beside' the harvesters, not among them, as a hint that בית דוד's kingdom would be divided.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she sat beside the harvesters.' רבי אלעזר said: Beside the harvesters, and not among the harvesters. He hinted to her that the kingship of בית דוד would be divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the verse, and רבי אלעזר reads her seating place as another hint about the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exact wording 'מצד' (at the side) instead of 'בתוך' (in the middle) is the trigger. Being off to the side hints that her descendants would not rule all of ישראל forever. The kingdom split after שלמה into יהודה and the ten tribes.

phrases.english: "And she sat beside the harvesters"
Rabbi Elazar said:
Beside the harvesters, and not among the harvesters,
he hinted a hint to her
that the kingship of the House of David will in the future be divided.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִצַּד הַקּוֹצְרִים וְלֹא בְּתוֹךְ הַקּוֹצְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through the same verse with another hint about בית דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Beside, not among' hints that the kingdom of בית דוד will be divided.

steps.title: Ate, satisfied, left over: דוד, שלמה, חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר maps the three verbs 'she ate, she was satisfied, she left over' onto three great kings descended from רות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he handed her roasted grain and she ate.' רבי אלעזר said: 'She ate' means in the days of דוד; 'she was satisfied' means in the days of שלמה; 'she left over' means in the days of חזקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the verse, and רבי אלעזר reads its three verbs as three stages of greatness in רות's royal family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each verb shows more abundance than the one before it: eating, then being full, then having extra. These match דוד, then שלמה (a time of peace and wealth), then חזקיה (a time of great Torah learning).

keyTerms.meaning: חזקיה, a righteous king of יהודה

phrases.english: "And he handed her roasted grain and she ate."
Rabbi Elazar said:
"And she ate": in the days of David,
"and she was satisfied": in the days of Solomon,
"and she left some over": in the days of Hezekiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: ״וַתֹּאכַל״ — בִּימֵי דָוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same verse with a three-part prophetic reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three verbs correspond to דוד, שלמה, and חזקיה.

steps.title: Another version: the leftovers reach the days of רבי
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion shifts the mapping so that 'left over' refers to the days of רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: 'She ate' means in the days of דוד and שלמה; 'she was satisfied' means in the days of חזקיה; 'she left over' means in the days of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same three-part reading, with a different line-up of eras.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here דוד and שלמה share the first stage, חזקיה moves up to 'satisfied', and the highest stage, 'leftovers', is pushed to the time of רבי, who descended from בית דוד. The next step will explain why רבי's era counts as so abundant.

phrases.english: And some say:
"And she ate": in the days of David and in the days of Solomon,
"and she was satisfied": in the days of Hezekiah,
"and she left some over": in the days of Rebbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of רבי אלעזר's three-part mapping from step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three stages are דוד and שלמה, then חזקיה, then רבי.

steps.title: רבי's stable-keeper was richer than the Persian king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the claim about רבי's era: even רבי's stable-keeper was wealthier than שבור מלכא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: רבי's stable-keeper was richer than שבור מלכא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a known statement to show why רבי's time deserves the name 'left over'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a minor worker in רבי's household was richer than the king of Persia, then that era truly had more than enough. This backs up the 'leftovers' reading from step 31.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
Rebbi's stable-keeper
was richer than King Shapur.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 31 that רבי's days match 'she left over'.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי's era fits 'ותותר' (abundance beyond need).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known teaching ('אמר מר') that רבי's stable-keeper was richer than שבור מלכא.

steps.title: A ברייתא: this world, the days of משיח, and the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the three verbs as three spiritual eras: this world, ימות המשיח, and לעתיד לבוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: 'She ate' means in this world; 'she was satisfied' means in ימות המשיח; 'she left over' means לעתיד לבוא, the future to come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third reading of the three verbs from a ברייתא, now about world eras rather than specific kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of kings, the stages are three periods of history. Each step brings more blessing: this world, then ימות המשיח (the Messiah being a descendant of רות), then the final future.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The future to come (end of days)

steps.whatToRemember: The three verbs 'ותאכל, ותשבע, ותותר' get three readings: רבי אלעזר (דוד, שלמה, חזקיה), איכא דאמרי (דוד and שלמה, חזקיה, רבי), and the ברייתא (this world, ימות המשיח, לעתיד לבוא). All agree the verbs show growing blessing among רות's descendants.

phrases.english: It was taught in a Baraita:
"And she ate": in this world,
"and she was satisfied": in the days of the Messiah,
"and she left some over": in the future to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, tannaitic reading of the same three verbs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verbs correspond to this world, ימות המשיח, and לעתיד לבוא.

steps.title: 'Under his honor': the body burned, not the clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads 'under his honor' in ישעיה as meaning that what was under the clothing burned, but not the clothing itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And under his honor a burning will burn like a burning fire.' רבי יוחנן said: 'Under his honor', and not his actual honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new verse about the destruction of the army of אשור, and רבי יוחנן explains the word 'under'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the fire burned 'under' his honor, not the honor itself. רבי יוחנן reads 'honor' as the soldiers' clothing. So their bodies, which are under the clothes, burned, while the clothes stayed whole.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a jump to a new topic. We are no longer in מגילת רות. The verse is from ישעיה and is about the army of סנחריב, king of אשור.

phrases.english: "And under his honor a burning will burn like the burning of fire."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
"And under his honor,"
and not his actual honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: ״וְתַחַת כְּבוֹדוֹ״, וְלֹא כְּבוֹדוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רות passage and returns to the earlier theme of clothing as 'honor'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only what was under the 'honor' (the clothing) burned. The clothing itself was not burned.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows his own view that clothes are 'honor'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's reading fits his own habit of calling his clothes 'my honorers'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, for רבי יוחנן called his clothes 'my honorers'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רבי יוחנן read 'כבודו' as clothing: it matches how he himself spoke about his clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לטעמיה' means a sage is being consistent with his known view. Since רבי יוחנן called his clothes 'מכבדותי' (the things that honor me), it makes sense that he reads 'honor' in the verse as clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: My honorers (the things that give me honor)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to the earlier theme on this דף, that שבת clothing should be different and dignified, because clothing gives a person כבוד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
for Rabbi Yochanan called his clothes "my honorers."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source of רבי יוחנן's reading in step 34 by pointing to his own consistent usage.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading of 'כבודו' as clothing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own practice of calling his clothes 'מכבדותי'.

steps.title: The body itself was burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'under his honor' as 'in place of his real honor.' The body itself burned up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: 'And under his honor' means in place of his actual honor. The body itself, which is his honor, was burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second reading of 'תחת כבודו.' רבי אלעזר says the 'honor' is the person's body, and that is what burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן read 'honor' as the clothing and 'under' as what lies beneath it. רבי אלעזר reads 'תחת' as 'in place of.' So where the body, the person's real honor, used to be, only ashes remained.

keyTerms.meaning: Can mean 'under' or 'in place of.' The argument depends on which meaning is used.
His honor. Here רבי אלעזר says it means the body itself.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the opinions. For רבי יוחנן, 'honor' means the clothes, and the clothes survived. For רבי אלעזר, 'honor' means the body itself, and the body was burned.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
"And under his honor" means
phrases.notes: Quoting the verse in ישעיה about סנחריב's army.

phrases.english: in place of his actual honor.
phrases.notes: The body is his honor, and it was burned up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reading that differs from רבי יוחנן's reading in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'תחת כבודו' means 'in place of his real honor.' The body itself was burned.

steps.title: The soul was burned but the body stayed whole
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני compares the army's burning to the death of בני אהרן. The soul burned while the body stayed intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: 'Under his honor' means like the burning of the sons of אהרן. There, the soul was burned while the body stayed intact. So too here, the soul was burned while the body stayed intact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third reading of the verse. רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the burning was inside the body, just like with נדב and אביהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses a comparison: 'מה להלן... אף כאן', meaning 'just as there... so too here.' בני אהרן died by fire from Heaven, yet their bodies stayed whole. So סנחריב's soldiers also died with their souls burned while their bodies remained. This is the opposite of רבי אלעזר, who said the body itself burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The sons of אהרן, נדב and אביהו. They died by fire from Heaven in the משכן.
'Just as there... so too here.' This is the formula for comparing two cases.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on 'תחת כבודו.' רבי יוחנן: the body burned, but the clothes did not. רבי אלעזר: the body itself burned. רבי שמואל בר נחמני: the soul burned, and the body stayed whole.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
"Under his honor" means
phrases.notes: Here it means beneath the flesh, deep inside.

phrases.english: like the burning of the sons of Aaron.
Just as there, it was a burning of the soul
while the body remained intact,
so too here, it was a burning of the soul
while the body remained intact.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading, which disagrees with רבי אלעזר's view that the body burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The soldiers died like בני אהרן: their souls were burned and their bodies stayed whole.

steps.title: Opening a new teaching of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר אבא begins quoting a new statement in the name of רבי יוחנן. The statement itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is introducing who is speaking, and the actual statement comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a chain of quotation. רבי אחא בר אבא is passing on what his teacher רבי יוחנן said. Nothing new is taught yet, so wait for the next line to see the content.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete thought. It only tells us who is speaking. The teaching itself begins on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of how the army burned to a new teaching. The attribution is given here because this passage ends mid-sentence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attribution only. The content follows on the next amud.
